RECURRENCE (2026-09-08): confirmed at the identical structural position across 20+ languages on this ONE page -- the 'Text Frames with FrameFormat' paragraph describes properties with the pattern 'X and Y ... report Z' (plural subject, bare verb form 'report', no -s), and the bare verb is mistranslated as an IMPERATIVE command instead of 3rd-person-plural-indicative. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED via live extraction trace (TextUnitExtractor.extract_from_ast on the real source file): the paragraph's single italic emphasis marker ('*current*') forces the ENTIRE paragraph into leaf-level extraction (_has_inline_formatting), fragmenting it at every code-span boundary. The bare-verb fragment ends up with NO visible subject (e.g. the unit is literally ', report where it is anchored relative to the page, margin, column, or paragraph; and' -- the subject 'HorizontalPosition and VerticalPosition, together with...' lives in separate CODE_SPAN units before it). English 'report' (bare form) is genuinely ambiguous between imperative and 3rd-person-plural without a visible subject; 'reports' (unambiguous -s form, e.g. 'IsFrame reports...') translates correctly in every locale for direct comparison. Thai is the only reviewed locale unaffected because it has no imperative/indicative mood distinction -- strong confirmation this is a genuine grammatical-ambiguity bug, not model variance. ARCHITECTURAL CONTEXT: this is the same class of bug TC-APT-013 (code spans) and TC-APT-036/076 (links) already fixed by excluding those inline elements from the leaf-splitting trigger in _has_inline_formatting; emphasis/bold appears to be the one common inline element NOT yet excluded. Those fixes each required a preserve_pattern + identity-round-trip validation across real pages before landing -- do not attempt the analogous emphasis exclusion without the same rigor (this note explicitly declines to guess at that fix). See data/summaries/fp-wave19-frameformat-imperative-verb-20260908.json for the full trace.

UPDATE to manual-wave24-blog-words-rb006-ar-enterprise-product and manual-wave24-blog-words-rb006-enterprise-product-multi-locale: the config/terminology.yaml fix (b801f275) was REVERTED this iteration (commit follows this one) after reverification against the exact originally-failing files surfaced a worse regression than the defect it fixed. Reverification manifest wave24-heal-words-rb006-reverify-20260909-r2 (ar/hu/ja/ro, professionalize_llm primary + m2m100 escalation) rejected ALL 4 cells with write_gate.py OVERWRITE BLOCKED: "Both existing (en) and new (en) are wrong language. Expected ar" -- i.e. the output came back predominantly/entirely English, not just the Enterprise-Product phrase. Root cause of the SIDE EFFECT (traced via a single-cell debug run with full stderr capture, not guessed): src/translation_engine/governed_terms.py::governed_multiword_terms() reads config/terminology.yaml exact_matches AUTOMATICALLY and feeds it into the language-detection signal-stripping used by write_gate.py's overwrite-comparison AND (per its own docstring) the frontmatter technical-signal regexes -- adding 5 new terms there did more than register a validator rule, it also changed what counts as "language evidence" for these short link-text units. The existing "Document Object Model" precedent comment in the same file explicitly warns terminology.yaml ALONE is validation-only and is NOT sufficient for actual pre-translation masking ("the profile pattern alone demonstrably does not hold" / needs a PAIRED site-profile preserve_pattern) -- I registered the new terms in terminology.yaml but did not add the paired preserve_pattern, so the terms were never actually masked from the model, while simultaneously being stripped from language- evidence text, which is the worse of both worlds for a short, term-dominated text unit like this one. NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: implement BOTH halves together (site-profile preserve_pattern for actual masking, matching the Document Object Model pattern exactly) and reverify with a full run BEFORE trusting it, the same discipline that caught this one. Do not re-add the terminology.yaml-only entries without the paired preserve_pattern -- reproduced this exact regression once already, no need to rediscover it.

note: translation_rejected; error_count=1; internal_retries=0; validators=SemanticSimilarityValidator; codes=SemanticSimilarityValidator; exceptions=TranslationRejectedError; verdict=unknown; score=unknown; unit_fingerprints=none; issue_fingerprints=SemanticSimilarityValidator:error:generic:dc937b59892604f5:payload_sha256=none:numeric=none; verification_checks=none; verification_fingerprints=none; error_sha256=31d6793d5c781914bae05324fae9924a225cbb8550fe459d9e2c1c1128172996

CONFIRMED via direct TranslationEngine.translate_file() call (bypassing CampaignManifest.verify_environment, whose TM-fingerprint check is currently unwinnable -- the shared LMDB store is being written by peer campaigns faster than a manifest build+launch race can complete). This is a genuinely NEW defect class, not previously ticketed, discovered while investigating model_quality_residual_phrase_defects (TC-APT-102) -- this page has 2 fenced csharp code blocks, both containing the identical line "using Aspose.Words.Drawing.Charts;". BOTH blocks come back from translation as "using Aspose.Words.Drawing.Diagramme;" -- the C# namespace segment "Charts" (which must never be touched, it is inside a fenced code block) gets replaced with "Diagramme", the German translation of the word "Charts" as used LEGITIMATELY elsewhere on the same page as a markdown heading ("### Charts" -> correctly "### Diagramme"). The corruption is byte-identical across both code blocks (not independent per-call variance), which points to a deterministic lookup/substitution mechanism (most likely a Translation Memory hit keyed on the bare word, or a whole-document consistency/find-replace pass) rather than the LLM independently hallucinating the same wrong output twice. Confirmed NOT a reconstruction-stage bug: text_unit_extractor.py _extract_code_block (~line 1768) correctly creates code blocks as ONE do_not_translate=True unit with source_text=node.raw (the full verbatim code); ast_renderer.py renders CODE_BLOCK nodes from node.raw verbatim with no translation logic at all. So the leak happens somewhere between extraction and reconstruction -- dispatched a subagent to trace the exact mechanism in segment_translator.py / the TM layer (result not yet in when this ticket was opened).

BLAST RADIUS CONCERN (not yet measured): any page where a code identifier/namespace segment happens to share an EXACT word with translated prose elsewhere on the same page (e.g. "Table", "Document", "Page", "Form", "Color" -- all common English words that are also common C#/API identifiers) is a candidate for this same corruption. Given how common single-English-word class/namespace names are in Aspose's own API surface, this could be a meaningfully widespread, previously-undetected defect class -- StructureValidator only WARNS on code content mismatch today (not ERROR, see structure_validator.py _check_code_block_contents docstring: 'promotes to ERROR after production data shows <1% FP'), so it is plausible this exact corruption has been silently shipping in already-committed pages without being caught by the zero-defect gate battery as a hard rejection in some run configurations. This specific run DID reject on it under zero-defect policy (see data/campaigns/debug-codeblock-words-net-20260910/failure_metadata.jsonl and debug-codeblock3-words-net-20260910/, gate=StructureValidator) -- but worth confirming it always blocks and never silently passes in other configurations.

DO NOT attempt a fix until the subagent's root-cause trace lands and is read; this note exists so the confirmed reproduction is not lost if the investigation spans a session boundary.

Root cause found by static reading (subagent trace got interrupted twice by session boundaries; took over directly): src/translation_engine/reconstructor/ast_renderer.py ~line 726, TC-APT-078's _correct_cross_reference call was gated only on kind_value != "heading_text", with no check for unit.do_not_translate. _correct_cross_references() does a word-boundary regex replace of any heading's source text with its translation, across whatever text it's handed -- for a do_not_translate=True code unit, that text is the raw code content. \bCharts\b matches right after the dot in 'Aspose.Words.Drawing.Charts' (a dot is a non-word character), so the heading's 'Charts'->'Diagramme' translation got applied inside the code.

FIX (commit 57c6167a): added 'and not unit.do_not_translate' to the gate. ORIGINAL DEFECT (confirmed, both models, heal-pdf-docmgmt-cpp-pl-document-object-duplication): source 'built from a loaded `Document` object.' -> pl 'zbudowanym na podstawie zaladowanego obiektu `Document` object.' -- the noun 'object' appears translated (obiektu, before the placeholder) AND ALSO left as a bare English echo immediately after the placeholder.

PATTERN SEARCH: grep across the whole portfolio's English source pages for the same shape (prose ending in a backtick-masked identifier immediately followed by a short generic classifier noun -- object/instance/class/type/method/document/collection/value/field -- then a period) found 24 source pages with this exact shape. Narrowed to the 9 using the identical trigger word 'object' (matching the original exactly, not just the general pattern).

LIVE TEST (direct TranslationEngine.translate_file() calls, professionalize_llm, same model family as the original confirmed instance, target_lang=pl matching the original locale exactly) on 3 of those 9, all different families (cells/cpp, slides/python, email/python) from the original (pdf/cpp):
  1. cells-spreadsheet-management-cpp: '...through the same `Workbook` type.' -> '...przy uzyciu tego samego typu `Workbook`.' -- clean, no duplication.
  2. slides-presentation-management-python: '...through the `DocumentProperties` object.' -> '...za pomoca obiektu `DocumentProperties`.' -- clean, no duplication.
  3. email-message-parsing-python: '...into a standard Python `email.message.EmailMessage` object.' -> '...na standardowy obiekt Python `email.message.EmailMessage`.' -- clean, no duplication.

All 3 negative. In every clean case, Polish grammar put the noun BEFORE the placeholder (genitive/accusative construction: 'tego samego typu X', 'za pomoca obiektu X', 'standardowy obiekt X') rather than after it -- the exact word-order choice that structurally avoids the trailing-echo trap the original defect fell into. 0/3 reproduced the duplication, satisfying the first-principles record's own pre-committed falsifiability criterion ('if not [2+ recur], mark MODEL_LIMITATION_DEFERRED, no fix warranted').

CONCLUSION: this is genuine per-sentence LLM sampling variance on one specific sentence, not a systematic producer-side or general model-behavior bug. No code fix warranted. The RECURRENCE ESCALATION gate for this class is now clear on process grounds (investigated per the FP record's own plan, found non-recurring). target_lang: all 25 mission locales (25/25 independently confirmed by 5 parallel review agents)
note:
5 parallel rubric-review agents (25 locales total, 5 each) unanimously REJECTED all 25 completed translations of this page for the SAME defect: the 'Common Issues' table header row ('| Issue | Cause | Fix |') left 'Issue' and 'Cause' untranslated in every single locale while 'Fix' translated correctly -- 25/25 reproduction, RB-005's exact recurrence-across-locales test for a confirmed producer bug, not model variance.

ROOT CAUSE (commit 553de701): text_unit_extractor.py's _is_non_translatable checks the i18n template-string registry first (is_translate_eligible) and only falls back to the legacy single-word PascalCase heuristic (_is_technical_identifier, Strategy 2) when no registry entry exists. 'Issue' (5 letters) and 'Cause' (5 letters) both match that heuristic's single-hump pattern (capital + 3+ lowercase, e.g. same shape as real identifiers like 'Workbook') with no registry entry to short-circuit it, so both were classified do_not_translate=True and copied verbatim into every locale. 'Fix' (only 2 lowercase chars after the capital) falls below the heuristic's {3,} floor and was never protected -- purely incidental, not because it was handled correctly by design.

Also investigated (and ruled out as a false alarm) a second suspected instance: the page's OTHER table ('API Reference Summary', headers 'Class / Method | Description') showed the identical do_not_translate=True pattern for 'Description' at the extraction layer -- but this is NOT a bug. A pre-existing registry entry (table.header.description, approved) already resolves it via a SEPARATE short-circuit (_i18n_table_value, text_unit_extractor.py ~line 1949-1958) that sets do_not_translate=True AS A SIGNAL that translated_text was already correctly resolved via the table, not as 'protect as English'. It renders correctly in French only by spelling coincidence (French 'Description' is spelled identically to English), which is why a reviewer's visual scan initially miscounted it as unaffected -- direct extraction-layer testing (not just eyeballing rendered output) was needed to tell the two do_not_translate=True cases apart.

FIX: added table.header.issue / table.header.cause entries to config/i18n/template_strings/_registry.yaml (category=table_header, status=pending -- the same curated mechanism that already protects 'Description') plus a value for each of the 25 mission target locales. This makes is_translate_eligible return True for both words in table_cell_text context, so _is_non_translatable never reaches the PascalCase heuristic for them -- they now flow through normal MT translation exactly like 'Fix' already did (status=pending means no pre-baked table value is served yet; that's a deliberate, safe choice -- the model translates them normally, and the registry entries exist so future curation can promote them to approved/table-served once evidence accumulates, per the module's own documented workflow).

VERIFIED: 8 new regression tests (tests/regression/test_table_header_issue_cause_translation.py) plus the full existing 198-test classification/extraction/i18n suite, all green. Extraction-layer live check (logs/debug_table_header_extraction.py, transient) confirms do_not_translate flips True->False for both words on the exact originally-failing page. Did NOT attempt a full model-translation live-reverify -- the currently-running wave (PID 48812) holds the TM lease; this is also a deterministic classification change (not a model-behavior question), so the extraction-layer check is the correct verification for this fix.

STILL TO DO (next wake, once the TM lease is free): (1) retrigger regeneration for this page's 25 locales with the fix applied -- none of the 25 currently-written candidate files should be committed as-is (they all predate the fix); (2) portfolio-wide blast-radius audit -- one reviewer spot-checked and found the SAME '| Issue | Cause |' untranslated-header pattern in OTHER, already-existing pages/languages ('ar, bg, fr, etc.') during their review, meaning this may already be live on committed content, not just this fresh page. That audit was not run this session (same shape as the TC-APT-109 blast-radius work already done once this session -- reuse that methodology: grep committed translations for the literal string '| Issue | Cause |' or similar table-header shapes, cross-reference against source to confirm).
